summary: Modules print JSON results which the normal action plugin parses; all returned strings are marked Unsafe so Jinja2 in them isn't templated, protecting the control node, and the executor re-audits results from action plugins that fail to mark them.
questions: Why doesn't Ansible template Jinja2 expressions found in module output?
Could a compromised managed node inject code through module return values?
Do custom action plugins need to mark their results as unsafe?

answer_card.title: Module return values are Unsafe
answer_card.answer_md: Modules print JSON to stdout; the `normal` action plugin parses it. To stop a malicious managed node from injecting templates that run on the control node, all returned strings are marked **Unsafe** and emitted verbatim. Results from `_execute_module()` are marked automatically; action plugins fetching data other ways must mark it themselves, and the executor re-marks all results as a safety net.
